title: Transatlantic airfreight rates at highest level for four years
content:
Transatlantic airfreight rates have hit their highest level since December 2022, as peak-season demand and tightening capacity push prices up – although last week’s US aviation disruption appears to have had little additional impact.
According to Freightos, Europe-US rates jumped 12% last week, to $3.27 per kg, while China–North America prices rose 16%, to $9.25 per kg, already exceeding last year’s December peak of $8.
The increases predated the nationwide US flight .

There are plans to expand the Asyaport terminal, which is 75% owned by MSC, and 25% by the local Soyuer Group, and increase capacity from the current 2.75m teu to 4m teu by the end of the year.
